narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 59.7% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is only modestly above a coin flip, but it means the model judged failure more likely than passing, so the application was rejected.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing. You were in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. This was the single largest influence and pushed the prediction toward bar-exam failure. Your first-year class standing was also in the lowest decile, compared with an accepted-student average near the sixth decile, and it was the third most influential factor, also pushing toward failure. The second most influential factor was your LSAT score. At 33 it is below the accepted-student average of about 37, but in this prediction it was the top-three factor that pushed toward passing rather than failing.

To move forward, request a review if the process allows one and provide context for your early and third-year grades, especially any upward trend or extenuating circumstances. Consider academic-readiness coursework or a post-baccalaureate record that demonstrates law-school preparation, and discuss with an admissions adviser whether retaking the LSAT or applying to programs with more holistic review would strengthen a future application.
